adopted.scripts/run-parallel.py: taken as a POSIX sh port, scripts/run-parallel.sh, generalized from pnpm script names to <label>=<command> pairs — vet.sh is not escapable, so it must not require python3. Read later upstream changes for the orchestration idea and port by hand; the file itself never lands here.

adopted.scripts/export-github-item.ts: taken as a Python port, scripts/export-github-item.py — the algorithm tracks upstream, the HTTP client does not. undici strips Authorization across a cross-host redirect and ignores HTTPS_PROXY; stdlib urllib does neither, so _DropAuthOnHostChange and the proxy-bypass opener here answer failure modes upstream cannot have. Port behavior changes by hand — a file-level diff compares two languages and says nothing.

adopted.scripts/gh-export/: upstream's exporter is split across these modules; the Python port splits too, as scripts/gh_export/ (underscore — a hyphen is not importable), but along its own module boundaries, so a change here rarely lands in the same-named file. Same standing as the export-github-item.ts note: read a commit here for the behavior change and port it by hand, never vendor the files.

adopted.scripts/lib/gh-api.ts: taken as scripts/lib/github.py, which shares only the job (one `gh`/HTTP wrapper for every stdlib script). Upstream shells out to `gh api`; the port speaks HTTP itself through the proxy-then-direct fetch ladder, so pagination and GraphQL are written differently by necessity.

declined..github/: the source's workflows are its own stack's — pnpm CI, a release gate, Railway deploys — and this repo ships no CI at all, leaving it to the adopting project: /test-on-gh and /bootstrap-workflow-dispatch are the stubs it hydrates against its own workflows. Re-offer any workflow that turns out to be stack-agnostic.
